Name: Alexandra Example
Description: This is a deliberately long description for testing the CSV table. It contains enough text to exceed the normal cell width several times, so the collapsed view should truncate it while the hover tooltip still exposes the complete value.
Notes: The expanded row should grow vertically and wrap this note across multiple lines. It is intentionally verbose so the row height change is easy to see in the preview.

Name: Benjamin Longfield
Description: A second long field makes it possible to compare several expanded cells in one row and confirms that the row height follows the tallest wrapped value rather than only the first column.
Notes: Use the eye button in an overflowing cell to reveal the full content. The upward chevron collapses the row back to the compact one-line presentation.

Name: Clara Verylongtext
Description: This value also includes a long unbroken identifier: product-design-specification-version-2026-09-21-with-extra-detail-for-overflow-testing-abcdef0123456789. The layout should break it when the row is expanded.
Notes: Long values can come from descriptions, notes, identifiers, or URLs. Every cell keeps its complete value available through the hover tooltip while remaining compact by default.

Name: Diego Example
Description: A final sample row provides another realistic paragraph of text describing an operational process, its ownership, the expected outcome, and the follow-up steps needed after the data has been imported.
Notes: This row is useful for checking that expanding one row does not expand every row and that other rows remain compact until their own control is selected.
